column1: # EXCLUDED_CASES.tsv -- logtalk_iso (CASE granularity, inside the tests.lgt files; never the package file census, which reads EXCLUDED.tsv as excluded FILES): the conformance cases OUT of the published denominator, one row per case: group:case<TAB>CLASS<TAB>the case's own condition. Read by SCRIP scripts/util_logtalk_grade.py; shipped 3617 = denominator 3546 + Excl 71.

# THE RULING (Lon 2026-10-05, in-chat to the ceo, verbatim: "Mark the Windows dependent tests as Excluded." and "Mark the bounded-integer tests as Excluded."; ceo CEO-1519, CEO-1520). An excluded case is never run and never counted as pass or fail; every other case is in the denominator (Lon, CEO-1518: "We do want ALL test programs to run. We have NO expected failures. We expect to have ALL features.").

# WINDOWS_ONLY: the case sits in the :- if(...) branch this suite compiles only on Windows; the SAME case name's unix else-branch is graded. BOUNDED_INTEGERS_ONLY: the case runs only where integers are bounded; SCRIP is unbounded like SWI (ceo measured: bounded=false, no max_integer flag, 9223372036854775807 + 1 = 9223372036854775808).

# EXCLUSIVE_BRANCH and DOTLESS_FLOAT_READ (ceo CEO-1524, 2026-10-05, on the coo's ask): four if/else pairs expect opposite outcomes of one goal, so no engine passes both -- the exclusive-configuration class of the Windows and bounded rulings; FEATURE PRESENT is decided for the dialect branch of op_3 iso_op_3_10 and for '|' an operator (op_3 iso_op_3_21), and FEATURE ABSENT for ^/2 callable (bagof_3, setof_3: CEO-1526 reversed CEO-1524 -- no oracle has a callable ^/2) (util_logtalk_extract.RULED) and each sibling branch is an EXCLUSIVE_BRANCH row; lgt_number_34 and lgt_number_35 read 1e33 and 1E33 expecting syntax_error, while SCRIP's default reads a dotless float as SWI does (11 SWI suite programs depend on it) and the strict ISO reading is built under set_prolog_flag(iso, true) by the cfo.
# THE LIST IS A RECORD, NOT A MASK: the grader REFUSES a row naming no such case, a row whose case does not carry the condition its class names, and a case a guard takes out that no row names.

# BOUNDED_MAX_ARITY_ONLY (ceo CEO-1540, 2026-10-07: max_arity IS AN INTEGER, SCRIP follows ISO and GNU; landed by the cfo at SCRIP 4f612be5d): the case runs only where max_arity is not unbounded and is written for a system whose max_arity is SMALL; at SCRIP's 2147483647 it asks for a structure no declared heap holds, and the case's expected error is not the resource error an engine raises there.

# NO_ORACLE_ANSWER (Lon via the ceo, CEO-1696, 2026-10-11, RULES.md section Oracles, verbatim: "Exclude any program in which we have no way to get output from an oracle, or in which we do not know the answer."): the case's goal calls a Logtalk SYSTEM predicate -- logtalk_compile/1, logtalk_load/2 -- which every Prolog oracle answers with existence_error, so no oracle answers it. The twenty unicode/encodings _01/_02 cases (the cfo's Logtalk row, CEO-1689); their _03/_04 siblings are graded with the fixture loaded by the backend adapter (CEO-1695, lib_logtalk_sequenced.tsv).

# NO_ORACLE_ANSWER, the second evidence form (ceo CEO-1697, 2026-10-14, on the cfo's measurement; CEO-1695 (1) withdrawn): four unbounded cases assert that functor/3 BUILDS a term of arity 1844674407370909797907654848955145546336677616 (~1.8e45); swipl 9.0.4, whose max_arity answers unbounded, raises representation_error(size_t) on each goal, so no run reproduces the answer. max_arity stays INT_MAX (CEO-1540 reading B); lgt_unbounded_functor_03 (representation_error(max_arity) under an integer bound) stays graded.

# NO_ORACLE_ANSWER, the third evidence form (ceo CEO-1977, 2026-10-25, on the coo's bisect of the four Logtalk reds; amends CEO-1696 for these six rows): format_2 and format_3 tab_table_pip_0110_16, _19 and _20 assert the text a NEWER swipl lays out for a ~t fill point and a ~N+ column stop; the pinned oracle swipl 9.0.4 prints a different text for each (measured 2026-10-25, /usr/bin/swipl 9.0.4: _16 '^     abc  $', _19 '^  a b  c  $', _20 '^a  b   c  $'), and SCRIP prints swipl's since 766d6f14f, which TreallaTests issues_test1014 and issues_test1015 need. The assertion is a ref that is not the oracle's, so the answer is not known. test_gate_logtalk_column_stop_rows_disagree_with_swipl.sh runs swipl on every row of this evidence form and reds the row the day swipl agrees with its assertion.
